_status_values: UNBOUND  - omop_concept_id / placeholder codings outstanding; service FAILS READINESS
BOUND    - all required concepts bound and signed off by SNUH terminology team
RETIRED  - superseded by a newer concept_map version
_notes: TWO-LAYER BINDING.
'features' holds measurement PRIMITIVES: things an instrument or a clinician
actually observed. These carry real LOINC / SNOMED CT codes and are rebindable
per institution.
'derived' holds features COMPUTED from those primitives. These are deliberately
NOT bound to terminology. A computation over observations is not itself an
observation, and minting a local code for one produces a concept that looks bound
but that no other site can interpret. Worse, it hides the failure that matters:
two sites can hold the same nominal concept and compute it differently (trapezoid
vs sample mean, different resampling, different gap handling), the terminology
layer reports success, and the model silently receives a different quantity.
So each derived entry declares its input primitives, its parameters, and a
version-bearing local identifier. The EXECUTABLE transform lives in
app/derivations.py and is hashed into the model artifact at export. Readiness
gate 5 refuses to serve if the two disagree. That is what makes the artifact
portable across institutions: rebinding the primitives cannot change what a
derived feature means.
OMOP concept_id values are left null. Standard concept_ids are specific to an
OHDSI ATHENA vocabulary release; binding them from outside SNUH's own vocabulary
build would be a guess. SNUH's terminology team must populate them against the
release recorded in 'omop_vocabulary_version' and flip status to BOUND.

target.name: intraoperative_hypotension
target.description: Probability of an intraoperative hypotensive event (MAP below 65 mmHg sustained for at least one minute) within the prediction horizon following an arrhythmia episode.
target._anchor_note: Features are computed ONLY over [onset, onset + observation_window]. The outcome is evaluated over (anchor, anchor + horizon]. The derivation layer rejects any sample after the anchor rather than dropping it: at training time such a sample is outcome leakage, and at serving time its presence means the caller mis-timed the payload.

features.verify_reason: CRITICAL. LOINC 8478-0 does not distinguish invasive arterial-line MAP from oscillometric NIBP-derived MAP. These are different measurements at different sampling rates, and a model trained on beat-to-beat arterial data cannot be run on 3-minute cuff readings even though both bind correctly to this code. SNUH must pin the source device/method, not only the code.

Rhythm findings are SNOMED CT-coded, not LOINC. SNUH must supply both the observation concept and a concept for every value-set member. Any episode whose rhythm code falls outside the bound value set is rejected rather than mapped to 'other'.
features._value_set_note: SNOMED CT is a subsumption hierarchy and EHRs emit at varying specificity. Binding only a 'primary' concept means a payload carrying a more specific descendant (e.g. chronic or permanent atrial fibrillation under a generic atrial fibrillation binding) is rejected even though it clearly belongs in that bucket. Because the SDDC is air-gapped, no terminology server can be called at request time to test subsumption, so the descendant closure must be PRE-EXPANDED into 'includes' when SNUH binds this map. Record the vocabulary release and expansion date in '_expansion': a closure is only valid for the release it came from, and a later release adding concepts silently shrinks coverage.
features._unmapped_policy_note: 'reject' (default): a code outside the bound value set returns 422. Rationale: 'other' in training meant 'residual rhythms actually observed', not 'codes we failed to map'. If a binding breaks and everything lands in 'other', the model runs on garbage and nothing errors. 'map_to_other': unmapped codes fall into the 'other' member. Rationale: in a live theatre a 422 means no risk score at all for that episode. Whichever is chosen, the unmapped RATE is counted and exposed on /readyz - a rising rate is how a vocabulary update that broke the binding becomes visible.

features.verify_reason: 8507/8532 are long-stable OMOP gender concepts but must still be confirmed against the local vocabulary release.

derived_writeback._comment: If derived values are persisted back to the record for audit or reuse, this is how. FHIR: Observation.derivedFrom pointing at the source Observations, Observation.code from the local CodeSystem below, Observation.method naming the transform version. OMOP: write to MEASUREMENT with measurement_concept_id = 0 (the honest encoding for 'no standard concept exists', rather than a forced mis-mapping), the local URI in measurement_source_value, and a derived-value type concept in measurement_type_concept_id.

excluded_features._comment: Documented so exclusions stay reviewable decisions rather than oversights.
excluded_features.post_anchor_samples: Any MAP or HR sample timestamped after the prediction anchor. Rejected, not truncated: at training time these are outcome leakage; at serving time their presence means the payload was assembled with the wrong window.
excluded_features.vasopressor_administration: Drug administration during the observation window is both a treatment response to falling MAP and a strong predictor of it. Including it without an explicit causal framing produces a model that learns 'the anaesthetist is worried', which is not the same as predicting hypotension and does not transfer to a site with different practice patterns.
excluded_features.free_text: Operation and diagnosis strings are re-identifying and are not part of the payload contract.
excluded_features.identifiers: caseid / subjectid style research identifiers are never accepted from or returned to the EHR.
